name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

# Cancel in-progress runs on the same branch when a new push arrives.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true

jobs:
  # ── 1. Format ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      # rustfmt is a pure Rust binary — no C toolchain needed.

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt

      - name: cargo fmt --check
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  # ── 2. Clippy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  clippy:
    name: Clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: clippy

      - name: cargo clippy — deny all warnings
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

  # ── 3. Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config musl-tools && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      # The wasm32 + tract-onnx + musl target combination produces a lot
      # of build output. Free space up-front and at the end so subsequent
      # jobs on the same runner aren't squeezed by leftover artefacts.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          df -h
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost /usr/share/swift /usr/local/.ghcup \
            "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl,wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: build

      # Build the ingredient-ai WASM crate first so the larderly crate's
      # `scanner-wasm` feature can `include_bytes!` the resulting module.
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        run: |
          if ! command -v wasm-pack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -f
          fi
          wasm-pack --version

      - name: Build ingredient-ai WASM module
        run: make wasm-pack

      - name: cargo build — workspace (warnings as errors)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --workspace

      - name: cargo build — larderly with scanner-wasm feature
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

      - name: cargo build — musl static target (with scanner-wasm)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

  # ── 4. Rust tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rust-tests:
    name: Rust Tests
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [fmt, clippy]

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_test
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-test-session-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3000
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config postgresql-client && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: rust-tests

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --no-default-features --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;" || true

  # ── 5. Playwright e2e ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e:
    name: Playwright E2E
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [rust-tests]

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_e2e
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-e2e-session-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3001
      APP_PORT:              "3001"
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"
      # E2E runs ~80 tests sequentially from a single runner IP; the
      # default 30 mutations/min/ip would 429 mid-run. Effectively
      # disable the limit in CI — the limiter's behaviour itself is
      # covered by unit tests; the e2e job's job is the integration
      # glue. Per-test counts include retries (2x on failure) which
      # can push concurrent POSTs to surprising levels.
      RATE_LIMIT_MUTATIONS_PER_MIN: "100000"

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config curl postgresql-client && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: e2e

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --no-default-features --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      # E2E tests mock the scanner module (the JS dynamic import 404s
      # gracefully and the page falls back to its stub). Building without
      # `--features scanner-wasm` saves a second wasm32 + tract-onnx
      # compile per CI run; the Build job already verifies the feature
      # builds cleanly.
      - name: Build app binary
        run: cargo build -p larderly

      - name: Start app
        run: |
          ./target/debug/larderly &
          echo $! > /tmp/larderly.pid
          echo -n "Waiting for app"
          until curl -sf http://localhost:3001/health > /dev/null 2>&1; do
            printf '.'
            sleep 1
          done
          echo " ready"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: tests-e2e/package-lock.json

      - name: Install Playwright
        run: cd tests-e2e && npm ci && npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run Playwright tests
        run: cd tests-e2e && BASE_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test

      - name: Stop app
        if: always()
        run: kill $(cat /tmp/larderly.pid) 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: tests-e2e/playwright-report/
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_e2e;" || true

  # ── 6. Container build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  container:
    name: Container Build
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [build, rust-tests]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.base_ref == 'main'

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y docker.io && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - name: Build scratch container
        run: DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0 docker build -f Containerfile -t larderly:ci .

      - name: Smoke test — binary exists in image
        run: |
          # Verify /larderly is present in the scratch image by extracting it.
          # Running the binary directly requires env vars (config loads at startup),
          # so we check existence instead.
          docker create --name larderly-smoke larderly:ci
          docker cp larderly-smoke:/larderly /tmp/larderly-smoke
          docker rm larderly-smoke
          test -f /tmp/larderly-smoke
          echo "Binary is present in the container image"

## Database Schema

```sql
-- Enable trigram similarity for fuzzy recipe name matching
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- ─── Users ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE users (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    avatar_url   TEXT,                -- from OIDC provider, or Garage-stored override
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per identity linked to a user. A user can link Google +
-- email/password to the same account; for password rows `sub` holds
-- the lowercased email so a user can sign in case-insensitively.
CREATE TABLE user_identities (
    user_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'google' | 'password' | 'mock'
    sub      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- provider sub, or lower(email) for password
    email    TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (provider, sub)
);

CREATE INDEX ON user_identities (user_id);

-- Server-side sessions (preferred over stateless JWT for OIDC revocation support)
CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE INDEX ON sessions (user_id);
CREATE INDEX ON sessions (expires_at);  -- for cleanup jobs

-- ─── Ingredients ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE ingredients (
    id      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name    TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,    -- canonical name, lowercase normalised
    aliases TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'   -- AI output normalisation targets
);

CREATE INDEX ON ingredients USING gin(name gin_trgm_ops);       -- fuzzy search
CREATE INDEX ON ingredients USING gin(aliases);                  -- alias lookup

-- ─── Recipes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE recipes (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name        TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- Display name, preserved case
    slug        TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- URL-safe, e.g. "chicken-tikka-masala"
    name_normal TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- Lowercase + collapsed whitespace, for dedup
    created_by  UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Full-text + trigram indexes for search and fuzzy dedup
CREATE INDEX ON recipes USING gin(to_tsvector('english', name));
CREATE INDEX ON recipes USING gin(name_normal gin_trgm_ops);

-- ─── Remixes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE remixes (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    recipe_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    submitted_by UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    title        TEXT NOT NULL,        -- e.g. "Gluten-free version"
    description  TEXT NOT NULL,        -- What makes this remix different
    steps        JSONB NOT NULL,       -- [{"order": 1, "text": "..."}, ...]
    image_key    TEXT,                 -- Garage S3 object key, nullable
    rating_avg   NUMERIC(3,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rating_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX ON remixes (recipe_id, rating_avg DESC);

-- Ingredients for each remix, with quantities
CREATE TABLE remix_ingredients (
    remix_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    ingredient_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES ingredients(id),
    quantity      TEXT NOT NULL,       -- e.g. "400g", "2 tbsp", "a pinch"
    optional      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    PRIMARY KEY (remix_id, ingredient_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON remix_ingredients (ingredient_id);

-- Per-user ratings (one per user per remix)
CREATE TABLE remix_ratings (
    remix_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    stars      SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (remix_id, user_id)
);

-- Trigger: keep rating_avg + rating_count updated on insert/update/delete
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_remix_rating()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    UPDATE remixes SET
        rating_avg   = (SELECT AVG(stars) FROM remix_ratings WHERE remix_id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id)),
        rating_count = (SELECT COUNT(*)   FROM remix_ratings WHERE remix_id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id))
    WHERE id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id);
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_rating_update
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON remix_ratings
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_remix_rating();

-- ─── Larder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE larder_items (
    user_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    ingredient_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES ingredients(id),
    added_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, ingredient_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON larder_items (user_id);
```

### Key Query — Larder-filtered Recipe Search

```sql
-- Returns recipes where at least one remix can be made from the user's larder
SELECT
    r.id,
    r.name,
    r.slug,
    COUNT(DISTINCT rm.id)     AS remix_count,
    MAX(rm.rating_avg)        AS top_rating,
    (SELECT title FROM remixes
     WHERE recipe_id = r.id
     ORDER BY rating_avg DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_remix_title
FROM recipes r
JOIN remixes rm ON rm.recipe_id = r.id
WHERE
    -- At least one remix has all its required ingredients in the larder
    EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM remixes rm2
        WHERE rm2.recipe_id = r.id
          AND NOT EXISTS (
              SELECT 1 FROM remix_ingredients ri
              WHERE ri.remix_id = rm2.id
                AND ri.optional = false
                AND ri.ingredient_id NOT IN (
                    SELECT ingredient_id FROM larder_items WHERE user_id = $1
                )
          )
    )
    AND ($2 = '' OR to_tsvector('english', r.name) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $2))
GROUP BY r.id
ORDER BY top_rating DESC NULLS LAST;
```

### Key Query — Fuzzy Recipe Name Match

```sql
-- Returns existing recipes with similarity above threshold
-- Used before creating a new recipe to detect near-duplicates
SELECT id, name, slug, similarity(name_normal, $1) AS sim
FROM recipes
WHERE similarity(name_normal, $1) > 0.55   -- tunable threshold
ORDER BY sim DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

### Schema — Favourites & Recipe Books

```sql
-- ─── Recipe Follows ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- User follows a recipe (live reference — always shows current top remix)
-- No snapshot needed: there is no content to preserve, just a pointer.

CREATE TABLE recipe_follows (
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    recipe_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    followed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, recipe_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON recipe_follows (user_id);

-- ─── Remix Favourites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- User saves a specific remix. A snapshot of the content is stored at the time
-- of favouriting (or at the time of the last accepted update). This snapshot is
-- what is shown if the user chooses "keep as is" after an update or deletion.

CREATE TYPE favourite_status AS ENUM (
    'current',           -- snapshot matches the live remix (or user accepted latest)
    'pending_update',    -- remix was edited; user has not yet decided what to do
    'pending_deletion',  -- remix was deleted; user has not yet decided what to do
    'kept_snapshot'      -- user chose "keep as is" after an update or deletion
);

CREATE TABLE remix_favourites (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    remix_id        UUID REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
                    -- SET NULL on delete so we can still show the snapshot
    pinned_version  INT  NOT NULL,          -- remix.version at time of last snapshot
    snapshot        JSONB NOT NULL,         -- full remix content frozen at that version
    status          favourite_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'current',
    notified_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- when the notification was last sent
    resolved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- when the user acted on a pending status
    favourited_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (user_id, remix_id)              -- one favourite per remix per user
);

CREATE INDEX ON remix_favourites (user_id, status);
CREATE INDEX ON remix_favourites (remix_id) WHERE status IN ('pending_update', 'pending_deletion');

-- ─── Remix versioning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Add version tracking to remixes so we can detect when a snapshot is stale.
-- version starts at 1 and increments on every edit via trigger.
-- (Applied as an ALTER in a migration, shown here for clarity.)

ALTER TABLE remixes ADD COLUMN version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
ALTER TABLE remixes ADD COLUMN updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now();

-- Trigger: increment version + updated_at whenever a remix is edited
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bump_remix_version()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.version    := OLD.version + 1;
    NEW.updated_at := now();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_remix_version
BEFORE UPDATE ON remixes
FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (
    OLD.title     IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.title     OR
    OLD.description IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.description OR
    OLD.steps     IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.steps
    -- rating changes do not count as a content edit
)
EXECUTE FUNCTION bump_remix_version();

-- ─── Notification inbox ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A lightweight inbox for in-app notifications.
-- The notification fan-out (one row per affected user) is handled by a
-- server-side job triggered after remix update/delete, not a DB trigger,
-- to avoid locking the remixes table during writes.

CREATE TYPE notification_kind AS ENUM (
    'remix_updated',
    'remix_deleted'
);

CREATE TABLE notifications (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    kind        notification_kind NOT NULL,
    -- Denormalised payload so we can render the notification even after deletion
    payload     JSONB NOT NULL,
    -- e.g. { recipe_name, remix_title, submitter_name, favourite_id }
    read        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX ON notifications (user_id, read, created_at DESC);
```

## Authentication — OpenID Connect

### Strategy

OIDC is handled entirely server-side using the `openidconnect` crate (pure Rust, no C dependencies). Sessions are stored in PostgreSQL, referenced by an httponly cookie — no JWTs in the browser.

### Supported Providers

| Provider | Issuer URL |
|---|---|
| Google | `https://accounts.google.com` |
| Email + password | n/a — local Argon2id, see Manual Authentication below |

### Auth Flow

```
User clicks "Sign in with Google"
    │
    ▼
GET /auth/google/start
    Server generates PKCE code_verifier + code_challenge
    Stores state + verifier in a short-lived DB row (or signed cookie)
    Redirects user to Google's authorization endpoint
    │
    ▼
Google → GET /auth/google/callback?code=...&state=...
    Server validates state
    Exchanges code for tokens (using PKCE verifier)
    Fetches userinfo from provider's userinfo endpoint
    Looks up user_identities by (provider, sub)
    ├── Found → load existing user
    └── Not found → create new user + identity row
    Creates session row in DB
    Sets httponly, secure, SameSite=Lax session cookie
    Redirects to /
```

### Key Axum Routes (outside Dioxus router)

```
GET  /auth/{provider}/start     → build OIDC redirect URL, set state cookie
GET  /auth/{provider}/callback  → exchange code, create session, set session cookie
POST /auth/logout               → revoke session, clear cookie
```

### Crates

```toml
openidconnect = "3"           # OIDC/OAuth2 — pure Rust, no C deps
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false,
            features = ["rustls-tls", "json"] }   # HTTP to providers — rustls only
tower-cookies = "0.10"        # Cookie middleware for axum
```

### Account Linking

If a user signs up manually as `a@b.com` and later signs in with Google as `a@b.com`, the OIDC callback finds the existing email in `user_identities` and links the new Google identity to the existing user — no duplicate account. The reverse direction (Google first, then trying to register manually with the same email) is rejected at the registration handler so a stranger can't claim an existing account by guessing the email.

## Manual Authentication (email + password)

Users without a Google account, or anyone who'd rather not use one, can register at `/register`. Three fields: display name, email, password (min 12, max 128 — NIST SP 800-63B-flavoured rules, no required mixed case / symbols).

Passwords are hashed with **Argon2id** (default OWASP 2024 parameters: m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1) and stored as PHC strings in `users.password_hash`. The matching `user_identities` row uses `provider='password'` and `sub=lower(email)` so a partial unique index keeps the email space exclusive.

Sign-in errors return a generic "Wrong email or password" regardless of whether the email is registered — user enumeration would otherwise be trivial via timing or message wording.

A future PR adds passkeys (WebAuthn) on top, with passwords kept as a backup. Email-based password reset is wired through Resend (see `RESEND_API_KEY` in `.env.example`).

## Recipe Deduplication & Fuzzy Matching

This is a critical UX flow. The goal is to keep the recipe index clean while making it frictionless to submit remixes.

### Normalisation

Before any comparison, names are normalised:
1. Lowercase
2. Unicode NFKD normalisation
3. Collapse all whitespace to single spaces, trim
4. Strip leading articles ("a ", "the ", "an ")

## Favourites & Recipe Books

### Two Distinct Interactions

| Action | What it saves | Snapshot? | Notification on change? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Follow a recipe** | Pointer to the recipe — always shows the live top-rated remix | No | No — the top remix changes naturally as ratings shift |
| **Favourite a remix** | Full content snapshot of this specific remix at this version | Yes | Yes — notified on edit or deletion |

Both appear together in the user's **Recipe Book** page, organised however they choose (default: alphabetical by recipe name).

### Favourite a Remix — Snapshot Model

When a user clicks "Favourite" on a remix:

```
Server fn: favourite_remix(remix_id)
    Load remix from DB (title, description, steps, ingredients + quantities)
    Serialise to JSONB snapshot
    Insert into remix_favourites:
        pinned_version = remix.version
        snapshot       = { title, description, steps, ingredients: [...] }
        status         = 'current'
```

The snapshot is a self-contained record of the remix at that moment. It does not reference the live DB rows for ingredients or steps — it is a flat, renderable copy.

### Remix Update — Notification Fan-out

When a submitter edits their remix (title, description, or steps change — `trg_remix_version` fires):

```
After successful UPDATE on remixes:
    Server-side job (triggered inline, not a DB trigger):
        SELECT id, user_id FROM remix_favourites
        WHERE remix_id = $updated_remix_id
          AND status = 'current'

        For each affected favourite:
            UPDATE remix_favourites
            SET status = 'pending_update'
            WHERE id = $favourite_id

            INSERT INTO notifications (user_id, kind, payload):
                kind    = 'remix_updated'
                payload = {
                    favourite_id:  ...,
                    recipe_name:   ...,
                    recipe_slug:   ...,
                    remix_title:   ...,   -- new title
                    submitter_name: ...
                }
```

### Remix Deletion — Notification Fan-out

When a submitter deletes their remix:

```
Server fn: delete_remix(remix_id)
    Before deleting:
        SELECT id, user_id, snapshot FROM remix_favourites
        WHERE remix_id = $remix_id

        For each affected favourite:
            UPDATE remix_favourites
            SET status     = 'pending_deletion',
                remix_id   = NULL    -- FK is SET NULL on delete
            WHERE id = $favourite_id

            INSERT INTO notifications ...
                kind = 'remix_deleted'

    DELETE FROM remixes WHERE id = $remix_id
    -- The JSONB snapshot in remix_favourites is unaffected
```

### User Resolution — Three Choices

When a user opens their Recipe Book or notification inbox and sees a pending item, they are presented with:

```

│  📋 "Gluten-free Chicken Tikka Masala" has been updated         │
│  by username                                                    │
│                                                                 │
│  What would you like to do?                                     │
```

```
SET status       = 'kept_snapshot',

WHERE id = $favourite_id

UPDATE notifications SET read = true WHERE ...
```

## AI Ingredient Scanner (WASM)

> **See also:** [docs/ai-scanner-models.md](docs/ai-scanner-models.md) — step-by-step instructions for exporting the YOLOv8n ONNX model, uploading it to Garage, and verifying the scanner can load it. Read that first if you are setting up the model assets for the first time.

### Model Strategy

Running a useful ingredient identifier in the browser requires balancing model accuracy against download size. The recommended approach is a **two-model pipeline**:

**Model 1 — Object Detection (lightweight):**  
`YOLOv8n` (nano) or `NanoDet` quantised to INT8 (~3–5MB ONNX)  
Detects and localises individual items in a fridge/shelf photo.  
Returns bounding boxes + coarse class (fruit, vegetable, packaged-good, meat, dairy, etc.)

**Model 2 — Classification (per crop):**  
`EfficientNet-Lite0` INT8 quantised (~5MB ONNX)  
Fine-tuned on a combined dataset:
- [Open Images V7](https://storage.googleapis.com/openimages/web/index.html) — grocery/produce classes
- [Food-101](https://data.vision.ee.ethz.ch/cvl/datasets_extra/food-101/) — prepared foods
- Open Food Facts product image dataset — packaged goods

Combined model set totals ~10MB, loaded once and cached via the browser's Cache API.

**Fallback:** If confidence on any crop falls below 0.60, the user sees "I'm not sure — could this be...?" with top-3 candidates to choose from.

### WASM Integration

```
User opens Scanner component
    │
    ▼
Browser camera access (web-sys MediaDevices API)
    │
    ▼
Capture frame → downscale to 640×640 on CanvasElement
    │
    ▼
ingredient-ai WASM: run YOLOv8n → bounding boxes
    │
    ▼
For each box: crop → 224×224 → EfficientNet-Lite0 → class + confidence
    │
    ▼
Return Vec<IngredientSuggestion { name, confidence, bounding_box }>
    │
    ▼
Frontend overlays bounding boxes on the camera feed
User sees detected ingredients highlighted in real time
    │
    ▼
User taps "Add all" or deselects individual items
    │
    ▼
Server fn: normalise_ai_result(names: Vec<String>)
    Fuzzy-matches against ingredients.aliases + ingredients.name
    Creates new ingredient rows for genuinely new ingredients
    Returns canonical ingredient IDs
    │
    ▼
Ingredients added to user's larder
```

## Terms of Service — Key Clauses

These points must be clearly stated in the ToS so users on all sides — submitters and savers alike — understand what to expect.

### For Remix Submitters

> **You own your remixes, and you can edit or delete them at any time.** However, because other users may have saved your remix to their Recipe Book, be aware that:
> - If you **edit** your remix, anyone who has saved it will be notified and given the choice to update their saved copy, keep their original version, or remove it.
> - If you **delete** your remix, anyone who has saved it will be notified and given the choice to keep their saved copy or remove it entirely. Deleting a remix does not automatically remove it from other users' Recipe Books if they choose to keep their copy.
>
> Please edit and delete responsibly. Deliberately removing a recipe that others rely on is discouraged, though it remains your right.

### For Recipe Book Users

> **Saved remixes are personal snapshots.** When you save (favourite) a specific remix, Larderly stores a copy of that remix at that point in time. This means:
> - Your saved copy will continue to work even if the submitter later edits or deletes their remix.
> - If a remix you have saved is changed or removed, you will receive a notification in your Recipe Book asking what you would like to do.
> - If you take no action, your saved copy remains as-is until you choose to act on the notification.
>
> **Followed recipes** (as opposed to saved remixes) always show the current top-rated remix live. You will not receive notifications for followed recipes — the content simply reflects the community's current best version.

### Regarding Duplicate Recipes

> Creating a recipe with a name that is the same as or very similar to an existing recipe, with the intent of gaining additional visibility, is a violation of these Terms. Larderly reserves the right to rename, merge, or remove any recipe found to be in violation of this policy without prior notice.

### Content Moderation

> Larderly moderators may rename, edit, or remove any recipe or remix that violates these Terms, including duplicates, inappropriate content, or spam. Where possible, affected users will be notified using the same notification system described above.

### Server Functions

```rust
// crates/larderly/src/server/recipes.rs

#[server(CheckRecipeName)]
pub async fn check_recipe_name(name: String) -> Result<RecipeNameCheck, ServerFnError> {
    let pool = crate::db::pool::get().await?;
    let normal = normalise_name(&name);
    crate::db::recipes::check_name(&pool, &normal).await
}

#[server(CreateRecipe)]
pub async fn create_recipe(input: CreateRecipeInput) -> Result<RecipeCreated, ServerFnError> {
    let pool = crate::db::pool::get().await?;
    let session = crate::auth::session::require_session().await?;
    // Atomic: insert recipe + first remix in one transaction
    crate::db::recipes::create_with_first_remix(&pool, session.user_id, input).await
}

#[server(SearchRecipes)]
pub async fn search_recipes(
    query: String,
    larder_filter: bool,
) -> Result<Vec<RecipeCard>, ServerFnError> {
    let pool = crate::db::pool::get().await?;
    let user_id = if larder_filter {
        Some(crate::auth::session::require_session().await?.user_id)
    } else {
        None
    };
    crate::db::recipes::search(&pool, &query, user_id).await
}
```

Dioxus automatically generates typed client-side wrappers for every `#[server]` function. The frontend calls them as normal async functions — no manual HTTP code.

## Container Build

```dockerfile
# Containerfile

# ── Stage 1: Build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM rust:1.82-slim AS builder

# musl target for a fully static binary — no glibc runtime needed
RUN rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y musl-tools && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Cache dependencies separately from source
COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock ./
COPY crates/larderly/Cargo.toml crates/larderly/
COPY crates/ingredient-ai/Cargo.toml crates/ingredient-ai/

# Build a dummy main to cache compiled deps
RUN mkdir -p crates/larderly/src && echo "fn main(){}" > crates/larderly/src/main.rs
RUN cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly 2>/dev/null || true

# Now build the real source
COPY . .
RUN touch crates/larderly/src/main.rs
RUN cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly

# ── Stage 2: Scratch — only the binary ───────────────────────────────────────
FROM scratch

# TLS root certificates for outbound OIDC/S3 HTTPS calls (rustls needs these)
COPY --from=builder /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/

COPY --from=builder \
    /app/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/larderly \
    /larderly

EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/larderly"]
```

**Strict no-C-deps rules:**
- `sqlx` → `tls-rustls` feature, no `native-tls`
- `reqwest` → `rustls-tls` feature, `default-features = false`
- `openidconnect` → depends on `reqwest`, same constraint
- `aws-sdk-s3` → `rustls` feature
- Zero `openssl`, `native-tls`, or `ring` (prefer `aws-lc-rs` or `rustls` crypto)

## Database Schema

```sql
-- Enable trigram similarity for fuzzy recipe name matching
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;

-- ─── Users ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE users (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    avatar_url   TEXT,                -- from OIDC provider, or Garage-stored override
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- One row per identity linked to a user. A user can link Google +
-- email/password to the same account; for password rows `sub` holds
-- the lowercased email so a user can sign in case-insensitively.
CREATE TABLE user_identities (
    user_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    provider TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'google' | 'password' | 'mock'
    sub      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- provider sub, or lower(email) for password
    email    TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (provider, sub)
);

CREATE INDEX ON user_identities (user_id);

-- Server-side sessions (preferred over stateless JWT for OIDC revocation support)
CREATE TABLE sessions (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    revoked    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
);

CREATE INDEX ON sessions (user_id);
CREATE INDEX ON sessions (expires_at);  -- for cleanup jobs

-- ─── Ingredients ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE ingredients (
    id      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name    TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,    -- canonical name, lowercase normalised
    aliases TEXT[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'   -- AI output normalisation targets
);

CREATE INDEX ON ingredients USING gin(name gin_trgm_ops);       -- fuzzy search
CREATE INDEX ON ingredients USING gin(aliases);                  -- alias lookup

-- ─── Recipes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE recipes (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name        TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- Display name, preserved case
    slug        TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- URL-safe, e.g. "chicken-tikka-masala"
    name_normal TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,          -- Lowercase + collapsed whitespace, for dedup
    created_by  UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Full-text + trigram indexes for search and fuzzy dedup
CREATE INDEX ON recipes USING gin(to_tsvector('english', name));
CREATE INDEX ON recipes USING gin(name_normal gin_trgm_ops);

-- ─── Remixes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE remixes (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    recipe_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    submitted_by UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    title        TEXT NOT NULL,        -- e.g. "Gluten-free version"
    description  TEXT NOT NULL,        -- What makes this remix different
    steps        JSONB NOT NULL,       -- [{"order": 1, "text": "..."}, ...]
    image_key    TEXT,                 -- Garage S3 object key, nullable
    rating_avg   NUMERIC(3,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    rating_count INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX ON remixes (recipe_id, rating_avg DESC);

-- Ingredients for each remix, with quantities
CREATE TABLE remix_ingredients (
    remix_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    ingredient_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES ingredients(id),
    quantity      TEXT NOT NULL,       -- e.g. "400g", "2 tbsp", "a pinch"
    optional      BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    PRIMARY KEY (remix_id, ingredient_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON remix_ingredients (ingredient_id);

-- Per-user ratings (one per user per remix)
CREATE TABLE remix_ratings (
    remix_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    stars      SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (stars BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (remix_id, user_id)
);

-- Trigger: keep rating_avg + rating_count updated on insert/update/delete
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_remix_rating()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    UPDATE remixes SET
        rating_avg   = (SELECT AVG(stars) FROM remix_ratings WHERE remix_id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id)),
        rating_count = (SELECT COUNT(*)   FROM remix_ratings WHERE remix_id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id))
    WHERE id = COALESCE(NEW.remix_id, OLD.remix_id);
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_rating_update
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON remix_ratings
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION update_remix_rating();

-- ─── Larder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

CREATE TABLE larder_items (
    user_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    ingredient_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES ingredients(id),
    added_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, ingredient_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON larder_items (user_id);
```

### Key Query — Larder-filtered Recipe Search

```sql
-- Returns recipes where at least one remix can be made from the user's larder
SELECT
    r.id,
    r.name,
    r.slug,
    COUNT(DISTINCT rm.id)     AS remix_count,
    MAX(rm.rating_avg)        AS top_rating,
    (SELECT title FROM remixes
     WHERE recipe_id = r.id
     ORDER BY rating_avg DESC LIMIT 1) AS top_remix_title
FROM recipes r
JOIN remixes rm ON rm.recipe_id = r.id
WHERE
    -- At least one remix has all its required ingredients in the larder
    EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM remixes rm2
        WHERE rm2.recipe_id = r.id
          AND NOT EXISTS (
              SELECT 1 FROM remix_ingredients ri
              WHERE ri.remix_id = rm2.id
                AND ri.optional = false
                AND ri.ingredient_id NOT IN (
                    SELECT ingredient_id FROM larder_items WHERE user_id = $1
                )
          )
    )
    AND ($2 = '' OR to_tsvector('english', r.name) @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $2))
GROUP BY r.id
ORDER BY top_rating DESC NULLS LAST;
```

### Key Query — Fuzzy Recipe Name Match

```sql
-- Returns existing recipes with similarity above threshold
-- Used before creating a new recipe to detect near-duplicates
SELECT id, name, slug, similarity(name_normal, $1) AS sim
FROM recipes
WHERE similarity(name_normal, $1) > 0.55   -- tunable threshold
ORDER BY sim DESC
LIMIT 5;
```

```sql
-- No snapshot needed: there is no content to preserve, just a pointer.

CREATE TABLE recipe_follows (
    user_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    recipe_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    followed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, recipe_id)
);

CREATE INDEX ON recipe_follows (user_id);

-- ─── Remix Favourites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- User saves a specific remix. A snapshot of the content is stored at the time
-- of favouriting (or at the time of the last accepted update). This snapshot is
-- what is shown if the user chooses "keep as is" after an update or deletion.

CREATE TYPE favourite_status AS ENUM (
    'current',           -- snapshot matches the live remix (or user accepted latest)
    'pending_update',    -- remix was edited; user has not yet decided what to do
    'pending_deletion',  -- remix was deleted; user has not yet decided what to do
    'kept_snapshot'      -- user chose "keep as is" after an update or deletion
);

CREATE TABLE remix_favourites (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id         UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    remix_id        UUID REFERENCES remixes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
                    -- SET NULL on delete so we can still show the snapshot
    pinned_version  INT  NOT NULL,          -- remix.version at time of last snapshot
    snapshot        JSONB NOT NULL,         -- full remix content frozen at that version
    status          favourite_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'current',
    notified_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- when the notification was last sent
    resolved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- when the user acted on a pending status
    favourited_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (user_id, remix_id)              -- one favourite per remix per user
);

CREATE INDEX ON remix_favourites (user_id, status);
CREATE INDEX ON remix_favourites (remix_id) WHERE status IN ('pending_update', 'pending_deletion');

-- ─── Remix versioning ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- Add version tracking to remixes so we can detect when a snapshot is stale.
-- version starts at 1 and increments on every edit via trigger.
-- (Applied as an ALTER in a migration, shown here for clarity.)

ALTER TABLE remixes ADD COLUMN version INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;
ALTER TABLE remixes ADD COLUMN updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now();

-- Trigger: increment version + updated_at whenever a remix is edited
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION bump_remix_version()
RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.version    := OLD.version + 1;
    NEW.updated_at := now();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER trg_remix_version
BEFORE UPDATE ON remixes
FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (
    OLD.title     IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.title     OR
    OLD.description IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.description OR
    OLD.steps     IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.steps
    -- rating changes do not count as a content edit
)
EXECUTE FUNCTION bump_remix_version();

-- ─── Notification inbox ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A lightweight inbox for in-app notifications.
-- The notification fan-out (one row per affected user) is handled by a
-- server-side job triggered after remix update/delete, not a DB trigger,
-- to avoid locking the remixes table during writes.

CREATE TYPE notification_kind AS ENUM (
    'remix_updated',
    'remix_deleted'
);

CREATE TABLE notifications (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    kind        notification_kind NOT NULL,
    -- Denormalised payload so we can render the notification even after deletion
    payload     JSONB NOT NULL,
    -- e.g. { recipe_name, remix_title, submitter_name, favourite_id }
    read        BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE INDEX ON notifications (user_id, read, created_at DESC);
```

## Authentication — OpenID Connect

### Strategy

OIDC is handled entirely server-side using the `openidconnect` crate (pure Rust, no C dependencies). Sessions are stored in PostgreSQL, referenced by an httponly cookie — no JWTs in the browser.

### Supported Providers

| Provider | Issuer URL |
|---|---|
| Google | `https://accounts.google.com` |
| Email + password | n/a — local Argon2id, see Manual Authentication below |

### Auth Flow

```
User clicks "Sign in with Google"
    │
    ▼
GET /auth/google/start
    Server generates PKCE code_verifier + code_challenge
    Stores state + verifier in a short-lived DB row (or signed cookie)
    Redirects user to Google's authorization endpoint
    │
    ▼
Google → GET /auth/google/callback?code=...&state=...
    Server validates state
    Exchanges code for tokens (using PKCE verifier)
    Fetches userinfo from provider's userinfo endpoint
    Looks up user_identities by (provider, sub)
    ├── Found → load existing user
    └── Not found → create new user + identity row
    Creates session row in DB
    Sets httponly, secure, SameSite=Lax session cookie
    Redirects to /
```

### Key Axum Routes (outside Dioxus router)

```
GET  /auth/{provider}/start     → build OIDC redirect URL, set state cookie
GET  /auth/{provider}/callback  → exchange code, create session, set session cookie
POST /auth/logout               → revoke session, clear cookie
```

### Crates

```toml
openidconnect = "3"           # OIDC/OAuth2 — pure Rust, no C deps
reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false,
            features = ["rustls-tls", "json"] }   # HTTP to providers — rustls only
tower-cookies = "0.10"        # Cookie middleware for axum
```

### Account Linking

If a user signs up manually as `a@b.com` and later signs in with Google as `a@b.com`, the OIDC callback finds the existing email in `user_identities` and links the new Google identity to the existing user — no duplicate account. The reverse direction (Google first, then trying to register manually with the same email) is rejected at the registration handler so a stranger can't claim an existing account by guessing the email.

## Manual Authentication (email + password)

Users without a Google account, or anyone who'd rather not use one, can register at `/register`. Three fields: display name, email, password (min 12, max 128 — NIST SP 800-63B-flavoured rules, no required mixed case / symbols).

Passwords are hashed with **Argon2id** (default OWASP 2024 parameters: m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1) and stored as PHC strings in `users.password_hash`. The matching `user_identities` row uses `provider='password'` and `sub=lower(email)` so a partial unique index keeps the email space exclusive.

Sign-in errors return a generic "Wrong email or password" regardless of whether the email is registered — user enumeration would otherwise be trivial via timing or message wording.

A future PR adds passkeys (WebAuthn) on top, with passwords kept as a backup. Email-based password reset is wired through Resend (see `RESEND_API_KEY` in `.env.example`).

## Recipe Deduplication & Fuzzy Matching

This is a critical UX flow. The goal is to keep the recipe index clean while making it frictionless to submit remixes.

### Normalisation

Before any comparison, names are normalised:
1. Lowercase
2. Unicode NFKD normalisation
3. Collapse all whitespace to single spaces, trim
4. Strip leading articles ("a ", "the ", "an ")

## Favourites & Recipe Books

### Two Distinct Interactions

| Action | What it saves | Snapshot? | Notification on change? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Follow a recipe** | Pointer to the recipe — always shows the live top-rated remix | No | No — the top remix changes naturally as ratings shift |
| **Favourite a remix** | Full content snapshot of this specific remix at this version | Yes | Yes — notified on edit or deletion |

Both appear together in the user's **Recipe Book** page, organised however they choose (default: alphabetical by recipe name).

### Favourite a Remix — Snapshot Model

When a user clicks "Favourite" on a remix:

```
Server fn: favourite_remix(remix_id)
    Load remix from DB (title, description, steps, ingredients + quantities)
    Serialise to JSONB snapshot
    Insert into remix_favourites:
        pinned_version = remix.version
        snapshot       = { title, description, steps, ingredients: [...] }
        status         = 'current'
```

The snapshot is a self-contained record of the remix at that moment. It does not reference the live DB rows for ingredients or steps — it is a flat, renderable copy.

### Remix Update — Notification Fan-out

When a submitter edits their remix (title, description, or steps change — `trg_remix_version` fires):

```
After successful UPDATE on remixes:
    Server-side job (triggered inline, not a DB trigger):
        SELECT id, user_id FROM remix_favourites
        WHERE remix_id = $updated_remix_id
          AND status = 'current'

        For each affected favourite:
            UPDATE remix_favourites
            SET status = 'pending_update'
            WHERE id = $favourite_id

            INSERT INTO notifications (user_id, kind, payload):
                kind    = 'remix_updated'
                payload = {
                    favourite_id:  ...,
                    recipe_name:   ...,
                    recipe_slug:   ...,
                    remix_title:   ...,   -- new title
                    submitter_name: ...
                }
```

### Remix Deletion — Notification Fan-out

When a submitter deletes their remix:

```
Server fn: delete_remix(remix_id)
    Before deleting:
        SELECT id, user_id, snapshot FROM remix_favourites
        WHERE remix_id = $remix_id

        For each affected favourite:
            UPDATE remix_favourites
            SET status     = 'pending_deletion',
                remix_id   = NULL    -- FK is SET NULL on delete
            WHERE id = $favourite_id

            INSERT INTO notifications ...
                kind = 'remix_deleted'

    DELETE FROM remixes WHERE id = $remix_id
    -- The JSONB snapshot in remix_favourites is unaffected
```

### User Resolution — Three Choices

When a user opens their Recipe Book or notification inbox and sees a pending item, they are presented with:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  📋 "Gluten-free Chicken Tikka Masala" has been updated         │
│  by username                                                    │
│                                                                 │
│  What would you like to do?                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  [Keep my saved version]   [Update to latest]   [Remove]       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

(If deleted):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ⚠  "Gluten-free Chicken Tikka Masala" has been removed         │
│  by username                                                    │
│                                                                 │
│  What would you like to do?                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  [Keep my saved copy]                         [Remove]         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Keep my saved version / Keep my saved copy:**
```

SET status       = 'kept_snapshot',
    resolved_at  = now()
WHERE id = $favourite_id

UPDATE notifications SET read = true WHERE ...
```

The stored JSONB snapshot continues to be displayed as-is in the recipe book. A small "saved copy" badge distinguishes it from live content.

**Update to latest** (only available if remix still exists):

```
SET snapshot       = <new serialised snapshot>,
    pinned_version = <new version>,
    status         = 'current',
    resolved_at    = now()
WHERE id = $favourite_id
```

**Remove:**
```
DELETE FROM remix_favourites WHERE id = $favourite_id
UPDATE notifications SET read = true WHERE ...
```

## AI Ingredient Scanner (WASM)

> **See also:** [docs/ai-scanner-models.md](docs/ai-scanner-models.md) — step-by-step instructions for exporting the YOLOv8n ONNX model, uploading it to Garage, and verifying the scanner can load it. Read that first if you are setting up the model assets for the first time.

### Model Strategy

Running a useful ingredient identifier in the browser requires balancing model accuracy against download size. The recommended approach is a **two-model pipeline**:

**Model 1 — Object Detection (lightweight):**  
`YOLOv8n` (nano) or `NanoDet` quantised to INT8 (~3–5MB ONNX)  
Detects and localises individual items in a fridge/shelf photo.  
Returns bounding boxes + coarse class (fruit, vegetable, packaged-good, meat, dairy, etc.)

**Model 2 — Classification (per crop):**  
`EfficientNet-Lite0` INT8 quantised (~5MB ONNX)  
Fine-tuned on a combined dataset:
- [Open Images V7](https://storage.googleapis.com/openimages/web/index.html) — grocery/produce classes
- [Food-101](https://data.vision.ee.ethz.ch/cvl/datasets_extra/food-101/) — prepared foods
- Open Food Facts product image dataset — packaged goods

Combined model set totals ~10MB, loaded once and cached via the browser's Cache API.

**Fallback:** If confidence on any crop falls below 0.60, the user sees "I'm not sure — could this be...?" with top-3 candidates to choose from.

### WASM Integration

```
User opens Scanner component
    │
    ▼
Browser camera access (web-sys MediaDevices API)
    │
    ▼
Capture frame → downscale to 640×640 on CanvasElement
    │
    ▼
ingredient-ai WASM: run YOLOv8n → bounding boxes
    │
    ▼
For each box: crop → 224×224 → EfficientNet-Lite0 → class + confidence
    │
    ▼
Return Vec<IngredientSuggestion { name, confidence, bounding_box }>
    │
    ▼
Frontend overlays bounding boxes on the camera feed
User sees detected ingredients highlighted in real time
    │
    ▼
User taps "Add all" or deselects individual items
    │
    ▼
Server fn: normalise_ai_result(names: Vec<String>)
    Fuzzy-matches against ingredients.aliases + ingredients.name
    Creates new ingredient rows for genuinely new ingredients
    Returns canonical ingredient IDs
    │
    ▼
Ingredients added to user's larder
```

## Terms of Service — Key Clauses

These points must be clearly stated in the ToS so users on all sides — submitters and savers alike — understand what to expect.

### For Remix Submitters

> **You own your remixes, and you can edit or delete them at any time.** However, because other users may have saved your remix to their Recipe Book, be aware that:
> - If you **edit** your remix, anyone who has saved it will be notified and given the choice to update their saved copy, keep their original version, or remove it.
> - If you **delete** your remix, anyone who has saved it will be notified and given the choice to keep their saved copy or remove it entirely. Deleting a remix does not automatically remove it from other users' Recipe Books if they choose to keep their copy.
>
> Please edit and delete responsibly. Deliberately removing a recipe that others rely on is discouraged, though it remains your right.

### For Recipe Book Users

> **Saved remixes are personal snapshots.** When you save (favourite) a specific remix, Larderly stores a copy of that remix at that point in time. This means:

> **Followed recipes** (as opposed to saved remixes) always show the current top-rated remix live. You will not receive notifications for followed recipes — the content simply reflects the community's current best version.

```dockerfile
# Containerfile

# ── Stage 1: Build ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM rust:1.82-slim AS builder

# musl target for a fully static binary — no glibc runtime needed
RUN rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y musl-tools && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Cache dependencies separately from source
COPY Cargo.toml Cargo.lock ./
COPY crates/larderly/Cargo.toml crates/larderly/
COPY crates/ingredient-ai/Cargo.toml crates/ingredient-ai/

# Build a dummy main to cache compiled deps
RUN mkdir -p crates/larderly/src && echo "fn main(){}" > crates/larderly/src/main.rs
RUN cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly 2>/dev/null || true

# Now build the real source
COPY . .
RUN touch crates/larderly/src/main.rs
RUN cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly

# ── Stage 2: Scratch — only the binary ───────────────────────────────────────
FROM scratch

# TLS root certificates for outbound OIDC/S3 HTTPS calls (rustls needs these)
COPY --from=builder /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt /etc/ssl/certs/

COPY --from=builder \
    /app/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/larderly \
    /larderly

EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["/larderly"]
```

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

# Cancel in-progress runs on the same branch when a new push arrives.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true

jobs:
  # ── 1. Format ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      # rustfmt is a pure Rust binary — no C toolchain needed.

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt

      - name: cargo fmt --check
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

  # ── 2. Clippy ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  clippy:
    name: Clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: clippy

      - name: cargo clippy — deny all warnings
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

  # ── 3. Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config musl-tools && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      # The wasm32 + tract-onnx + musl target combination produces a lot
      # of build output. Free space up-front and at the end so subsequent
      # jobs on the same runner aren't squeezed by leftover artefacts.
      - name: Free disk space
        run: |
          df -h
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/share/boost /usr/share/swift /usr/local/.ghcup \
            "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY:-/opt/hostedtoolcache}" 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo apt-get clean 2>/dev/null || true
          df -h

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable
        with:
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl,wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: build

      # Build the ingredient-ai WASM crate first so the larderly crate's
      # `scanner-wasm` feature can `include_bytes!` the resulting module.
      - name: Install wasm-pack
        run: |
          if ! command -v wasm-pack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl https://rustwasm.github.io/wasm-pack/installer/init.sh -sSf | sh -s -- -f
          fi
          wasm-pack --version

      - name: Build ingredient-ai WASM module
        run: make wasm-pack

      - name: cargo build — workspace (warnings as errors)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --workspace

      - name: cargo build — larderly with scanner-wasm feature
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

      - name: cargo build — musl static target (with scanner-wasm)
        run: RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl -p larderly --features scanner-wasm

  # ── 4. Rust tests ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  rust-tests:
    name: Rust Tests
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [fmt, clippy]

    env:
      DATABASE_URL:          postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/larderly_github_${{ github.run_id }}_test
      SESSION_SECRET:        ci-test-session-secret-not-used-in-production-000000000000
      APP_BASE_URL:          http://localhost:3000
      S3_ENDPOINT:           ${{ vars.S3_ENDPOINT }}
      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
      S3_ASSETS_BUCKET:      ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BUCKET }}
      S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET:     ${{ vars.S3_UPLOADS_BUCKET }}
      S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL:    ${{ vars.S3_ASSETS_BASE_URL }}
      OIDC_MOCK:             "true"

    steps:
      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: |
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential pkg-config postgresql-client && break
            echo "apt-get attempt $i failed; retrying in 10 s..."
            sleep 10
          done

      - name: Create test database
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "CREATE DATABASE larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;"

      - uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd  # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8  # stable

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@42dc69e1aa15d09112580998cf2ef0119e2e91ae  # v2
        with:
          shared-key: rust-tests

      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --no-default-features --features rustls,postgres

      - name: Run migrations
        run: cargo sqlx migrate run

      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --workspace

      - name: Drop test database
        if: always()
        run: |
          ADMIN="postgres://${{ vars.DB_USER }}:${{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@${{ vars.DB_HOST }}:${{ vars.DB_PORT }}/postgres"
          psql "$ADMIN" -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS larderly_github_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}_test;" || true

      S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID:      ${{ secrets.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
      S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:  ${{ secrets.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}

# Ollama Monitor

A Rust-based monitoring tool for Ollama that collects GPU and model information and exposes it via a REST API and web dashboard. Designed for later Home Assistant integration.

All configuration is via **environment variables** — no config files needed — making it easy to deploy with systemd or Docker.

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐
│  Ollama (localhost)    │  :11434/api/*       │      │                  │
└─────────────────┘ ─────│ ollama_monitor   │
                          │  (Rust + Axum)   │
┌─────────────────┐     ─┤                  │
│  nvidia-smi CLI  │◄────│                  │
│  (same host GPU) │     └──┬───┬───┬──────┘
└─────────────────┘        │   │   │
                          ▼   ▼   ▼
                     ┌──────────────────┐
                     │  REST API + Web   │
                     │  :3000/api/*      │
                     │  :3000/ (portal)  │
                     └──────────────────┘
```

## Systemd Service Deployment

To run `ollama_monitor` as a persistent background service:

### 1. Install the binary

```bash
sudo cp ./target/release/ollama_monitor /usr/local/bin/
sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/ollama_monitor
```

### 2. Create a systemd service unit with environment variables

Create `/etc/systemd/system/ollama_monitor.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Ollama Monitor
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ollama_monitor
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
Environment=RUST_LOG=info
Environment=OLLAMA_HOST=http://127.0.0.1
Environment=OLLAMA_PORT=11434
Environment=SERVER_BIND=0.0.0.0
Environment=SERVER_PORT=3000
Environment=REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECS=15
Environment=GPU_DEVICE_INDEX=0
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
User=root
Group=root

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

### 3. Enable and start the service

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable ollama_monitor
sudo systemctl start ollama_monitor
```
